question.leadin: Name some noteworthy popes of the Catholic Church.
question.text: This pope called for the First Crusade and offered a remission of sins for those who would participate in it.
question.answerHtml: Pope Urban II [accept Odo of Chatillon or Otho de Lagery; prompt on Urban]
question.clue: This pope allied himself with Roger I of Sicily, and he was heavily influenced by a delegation sent by Alexius I Komnenos.

swap.text: This Ecumenical Council from 1545 to 1563 was the Catholic Church's response to the Protestant Reformation.
swap.clue: This event, which resulted in the production of the Roman Catechism, lasted for twenty-five sessions under Paul III, Julius III, and Pius IV.

question.leadin: It was defined as the official Roman Catholic Dogma in the 1854 bull Ineffabilis Deus.
question.text: Identify this concept which states that Mary, the mother of Jesus, originated free from original sin.
question.clue: That bull, Ineffabilis Deus, was issued on the day of the "Feast" of this doctrine - December 8th - by Pope Pius IV.

swap.leadin: The Ku Klux Klan offered to assist the Mexican government in its conflict with this institution.
swap.text: Name this institution which was targeted by the administration of Plutarco Elias Calles [caye-yes], triggering the Cristero [Kris-tair-oh] War. This institution's leader was angered by the passage of Mexico's Reform Laws.
swap.clue: This institution was stripped of property by the Lerdo Law, which was opposed by Conservative leader Felix Zuloaga during the Reform War in Mexico.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about people and things that Martin Luther didn't like.
question.text: Luther's 95 Theses criticize the sale of these documents which offered to absolve sins of the living or dead. Johann Tetzel notably sold these documents in Germany.
question.clue: They were first granted en-masse during the Council of Clermont for those soldiers who set out to the Levant.

swap.text: In 452, Emperor Valentinian III sent this pope to meet with Attila near Mantua, where this pope legendarily convinced him to turn back. This pope also issued a namesake tome following the Council of Chalcedon.
swap.clue: While the filioque wasn't added to the Nicene Creed until the Council of Toledo, it was first proposed in the Tome of this Pope who declared the second council of Ephesus to be a "robber synod". This pope also convinced Valentinus III to declare Rome the head of the church and met with Atilla the Hun.

question.text: Calling upon Christians to retain orthodoxy and submission to the church, Robert the Monk records that a certain pope cried this phrase at the Council of Clermont, translating to "God wills it."
question.answerHtml: Deus Vult [accept Deus lo Vult or Deus le Vult; some players may pronounce the “V” as a “W” due to classical Latin pronunciation]

swap.text: Savonarola was excommunicated and later executed under the order of this Borgia pope, who also organised the Banquet of Chestnuts.
swap.clue: Cem Sultan was ultimately released by this man as a condition in negotiations with Charles VIII.

question.leadin: It followed the ineffectual rule of Benedict XI.
question.text: Name this period officially lasting from 1309 to 1377 that was resolved in the Council of Constance, in which several popes generally took up residence in a certain French city.
question.clue: The man who ended this time period did so after reading a letter written by Catherine of Siena.

swap.text: The victorious confederation at Lepanto, led by Don Juan of Austria, was known by this name due to the participation of the Papal States.
swap.clue: One of the members of a better-known group of this name won an important battle at Guinegate, also known as the Battle of the Spurs, and two year prior it defeated French forces at the battle of Novarra.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Great Schism of the West per part.
question.text: At the Council of Constance, this man was elected as sole holder of the papacy, thus ending the schism.
question.clue: This man was elected pope during the 1417 Council of Constance. The successor to Gregory XII, he ruled until 1431 when he was succeeded by Eugene IV.

swap.text: This dogma, that the pope cannot err when speaking in his official role as pontiff, was propounded at the First Vatican Council.
swap.clue: What is the two-word name in English for the idea that the pope speaks for the whole church and cannot be in error?

question.leadin: This Pope initiated the first crusade in 1095.
question.text: Name this pope, born Odo of Chatillon, who received Alexios I's appeal for aid against the Seljuk Turks.
question.clue: This leader wrote a letter of instruction to the Flemish mentioning Adhemar of Le Puy, as reported on by Baldric of Dol and Robert the Monk.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the year 1968.
swap.text: In July, this pope issued the encyclical Humanae vitae, which condemned artificial birth control. In 1968, this pope who closed the Second Vatican Council also beatified the Korean Martyrs.
swap.answerHtml: Paul VI (or Giovanni Battista Enrico Antonio Maria Montini)
swap.clue: This pope who canonized the Uganda martyrs and later visited Kampala in 1969 in the first papal trip to Africa. This pope presided over the end of Vatican II after the death of John XXIII ("the twenty-third").

question.leadin: An attempt to end this period at the conciliabolo, or "secret meeting," ended up creating a third faction by electing Alexander V.
question.text: Name this period in which two, then three, people simultaneously laid claim to the papacy. The 1409 Council of Pisa failed to end this period.
question.answerHtml: Western Schism [accept Schism of 1378; accept Papal Schism; accept Great Occidental Schism]
question.clue: Pierre d'Ailly ("dah-YEE") and Jean Gerson ("zhawn zhair-SON") promoted a conciliar resolution to this conflict, which began when 13 rebels staged an election in Fondi ("FOHN-dee") with regalia stolen by a camerlengo.

swap.text: The 1893 general strike, which accelerated socialism in Belgium, was sparked in part by the passage of this papal encyclical issued by Leo XIII, named in English for the "Rights and Duties of Capital and Labor."
swap.clue: This encyclical promulgated by Pope Leo XIII, which addresses workers' rights. It rejected both Communism and unbridled free-market capitalism.

question.text: The seizure of this six-year-old from his Jewish parents on Pius IX's watch, on the rumor that he had been baptized by his nanny, became a cause celebre for opponents of Papal rule.

swap.leadin: In 1303 armed forces of Philip IV stormed into the pope's residence and took him prisoner with the help of a powerful Italian noble, who reputedly slapped the pope in the face.
swap.text: Identify this event, named for the town in which the pope was imprisoned for three days.

question.leadin: Michaelist sources, such as The Chronicle of Nicholas the Minorite, were cited as proof of the intransigency of this Pope during the Apostolic Poverty Controversy. FTPE.
question.text: Name this Pope during the Avignon Papacy who succeeded Clement V in 1316. He quarreled with Emperor Louis IV of Bavaria, who under advice of William of Ockham, set up the antipope Nicholas V.

swap.text: This pope got Henry III into all that trouble by enticing him to take the throne of Sicily. He succeeded Celestine IV after an 18-month vacancy in the pontificate and called the Council of Lyons which excommunicated Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II.
